data.title: Information panels at Dolné Orešany – Slepý vrch
data.excerpt: On 13 June 2015 our Hradiská civic association installed two information panels about the Celtic hillfort known as Slepý vrch at Dolné Orešany. The re-enactment group Vae Victis set up a period Celtic camp on the hillfort, and the archaeologist Matúš Sládok spoke about the looting of archaeological sites and their protection.

mediaTexts.alt: A group of people installing an information panel at the edge of the village, a wheelbarrow of mortar in the foreground

children.text: On 13 June 2015 another event of our Hradiská civic association took place – the installation of two information panels at Dolné Orešany concerning the Celtic hillfort known as Slepý vrch.

We met with an exceptionally helpful attitude on the part of the mayor of Dolné Orešany, Mrs Juliana Belicová, who not only promised to finance both panels but also, together with the municipal office and other residents, gave us wonderful support, thanks to which a great many people came to the event and the atmosphere was splendid.

First we installed the first panel in the centre of the village, near the municipal office; on it visitors can learn about the existence of the hillfort on Slepý vrch and read about the earliest occupation of Dolné Orešany in prehistory. A speech was also given to those present by the archaeologist of the Regional Monuments Board in Trnava, Mgr. Matúš Sládok, who among other things spoke about the problem of the looting of archaeological sites and about their protection.

blocks.alt: Information panels at Dolné Orešany - Slepý vrch

children.text: We then moved directly to the Slepý vrch hillfort, where a surprise awaited the visitors – the Celts. Our invitation had in fact been accepted by
the renowned group devoted to bringing Celtic history to life – Vae Victis from Lietavská Lúčka

. On the hillfort they had set up a period camp and a weaving loom and, of course, they themselves were dressed as Celts with the appropriate equipment. They showed us the Celtic way of life, told us about it engagingly, and at the end their druid Brendyx blessed our panel with mead, so that it might long serve the glory of the Celtic gods.

The journey up to the hillfort with a panel on one's shoulder would have been extremely demanding, and so I must highlight the enormous help of Mr Lukáš Ilavský of Dolné Orešany, who brought all the necessary material up to the hillfort, and also of Patrik Dobšovič, who saw to transporting the Celts and their equipment up there.

Despite the hot weather a large number of interested people came to the hillfort. At the end they were able to watch several paragliders take off from Slepý vrch, whose participation was likewise arranged by the mayor. After returning to the village we had excellent goulash and refreshments ready at the municipal office.

At this point I would like to thank everyone who took part in making the panel (our lads from the association), the Vae Victis group for its great contribution, but above all the mayor for her helpfulness. We have never met with such a splendid attitude. And, of course, the residents of Orešany, who are not indifferent to their history and who came in large numbers to support us.
We look forward to the next event.
